title: Dialysis Water Loop Test Failure — Do Not Drink Advisory

fields.organization: Ottawa River Regional Medical Center — Dialysis Operations
fields.location: Outpatient Dialysis Center — Water Treatment Room, Central Plant (Room C-B03)
fields.inspector: T. Kline, Dialysis Water Treatment Technician
fields.summary: Test results indicate the dialysis water loop has failed due to elevated chlorine levels. Total chlorine at the carbon bed outlet is 0.35 mg/L, exceeding the 0.1 mg/L limit for dialysis. Conductivity at the RO outlet is normal (8 microsiemens). The second carbon bed is in line and the filter was replaced Tuesday, March 14. The city water entering the plant has a stronger chlorine odor than usual. The loop cannot be used for dialysis. Patient treatments must be postponed.

findings.item: Total chlorine level at carbon bed outlet

findings.notes: Second bed in line; filter replaced 03/14/2026
City main inlet, no visible contamination

actionsTaken: Notified NEPH and DFEM via intercom at 06:44
Closed manual isolation valve on RO feed line
Logged test results in HCC system (DWR-2026-0314-0644-001)
Initiated emergency call to patients with transport coordination
recommendations: Immediate suspension of all outpatient dialysis using city water feed
Submit water sample to Toledo-Lucas County Health Department for analysis (via EMA)
Notify Lucas County EMS of pending patient transport
Review RO maintenance logs for pattern of carbon bed performance
fields.photosNote: 4 photos attached: IMG_DWR0644-01 to IMG_DWR0644-04 (chlorine test vial, RO outlet reading, carbon bed inlet, water odor assessment)
fields.signature: T. Kline, Dialysis Water Treatment Technician

instructorNote: This inject confirms the water loop failure and triggers the dialysis continuity protocol. Watch for NEPH to authorize halting the loop and for DFEM to initiate the sample submission. The failed chlorine level is a direct clue to the city water issue, not a system fault.
